name: Corselet-gorge
summary: A garment that holds the bust on its own, apart from the corset below it, so that the weight rests on the shoulders and not on the waist.
how: Cut the support as a separate piece with two cups and a back band.
Hang the cups from two shoulder straps.
Fasten the band at the back with hooks or ties.

origin.note: Herminie Cadolle files a patent for a corset that is cut into a lower corset and an upper bust support.

adoptions.via: Mary Phelps Jacob patented a light backless brassière of two handkerchiefs and ribbon, with no corset.
A maker of brassières founded in 1922 sold the separate bust support in sizes.
